### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.surround

### Question

I use the keybind `ds` to delete surroundings. This seems to be directly mapped in normal mode, which has the consequence of preventing Neovim from going into operator-pending mode when I press `d`. I wanted to see if I could create a mapping in operator-pending mode using `vim.g.operator` to fix this. I see there is a `MiniSurround.delete()` function, but it doesn't seem to wait for the user to input the surrounding to delete.

Is there a correct way to manually delete a surrounding using `MiniSurround.delete()`?

Right now I'm using a proxy binding and then mapping to it:

```lua
local mini_surround = require("mini.surround")
mini_surround.setup({
    mappings = {
        add = "s",
        delete = "\\sd",
        replace = "\\sc",
        ...
    },
})

vim.keymap.set(
    { 'o' },
    "s",
    function()
        if vim.v.operator == "d" then
            return "<Esc>\\sd"
        elseif vim.v.operator == "c" then
            return "<Esc>\\sc"
        end
        return "<Esc>"
    end,
    { expr = true, remap = true }
)
```

which works really well but is a little clunky.

Thanks!

comment_data.body:
### Why calling `MiniSurround.delete()` directly skips the prompt

In [`lua/mini/surround.lua`](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/lua/mini/surround.lua), `MiniSurround.delete` and `MiniSurround.replace` are `operatorfunc` callbacks, not standalone entry points. They rely on a module-local `H.cache` table for dot-repeat (`.`):

```lua
-- Inside H.get_surround_spec(surr_type):
H.cache.n_calls = H.cache.n_calls or { input = 0, output = 0 }
if not H.is_mc_cascade() then H.cache.n_calls[surr_type] = H.cache.n_calls[surr_type] + 1 end
if H.cache.n_calls[surr_type] <= 1 then H.cache[surr_type] = nil end

-- Reuses cached input on subsequent calls instead of prompting!
if H.cache[surr_type] ~= nil then return H.cache[surr_type] end
```

`H.cache` is only reset inside the private `H.make_operator()` wrapper that `MiniSurround.setup()` binds to your `mappings.*` keys:

```lua
H.cache = { count = vim.v.count1, search_method = search_method }
vim.o.operatorfunc = 'v:lua.MiniSurround.' .. task
return '<Cmd>redraw<CR>g@' .. (ask_for_textobject and '' or ' ')
```

When you call `MiniSurround.delete()` directly, `H.cache` is never reset — so after the first surrounding operation, `H.cache.n_calls.input > 1` and `H.cache.input` is already populated, causing `MiniSurround.delete()` to immediately reuse the previous surrounding without prompting. Because `H.cache` and `H.make_operator` are module-local (`local H = {}`), there is no public Lua function to reset `H.cache` manually.

### Cleaner alternative to `\sd` / `\sc`: use `<Plug>` mappings

`H.apply_config` passes `config.mappings.delete` and `config.mappings.replace` straight to `vim.keymap.set('n', lhs, H.make_operator(...), { expr = true })`. You can therefore use `<Plug>` names as the LHS instead of real key sequences like `\sd` / `\sc` — avoiding any normal-mode key collisions or `which-key` clutter while still keeping `H.cache` reset, `[count]`, and `.` dot-repeat working properly:

```lua
require('mini.surround').setup({
  mappings = {
    add = 's',
    delete = '<Plug>(MiniSurroundDelete)',
    replace = '<Plug>(MiniSurroundReplace)',
    -- Clear suffixes if you don't want '<Plug>(...)l' / '<Plug>(...)n' created too
    suffix_last = '',
    suffix_next = '',
  },
})

vim.keymap.set('o', 's', function()
  if vim.v.operator == 'd' then
    return '<Esc><Plug>(MiniSurroundDelete)'
  elseif vim.v.operator == 'c' then
    return '<Esc><Plug>(MiniSurroundReplace)'
  end
  return '<Esc>'
end, { expr = true, remap = true })
```

*(If you still want `last`/`next` variants, keep `suffix_last = 'l'` / `suffix_next = 'n'` and map `sl` / `sn` in `'o'` mode to `<Esc><Plug>(MiniSurroundDelete)l` / `<Esc><Plug>(MiniSurroundDelete)n`, etc.)*

comment_data.body:
`MiniSurround.delete()` doesn't prompt because it reads the identifier from an internal cache, and that cache is only reset by the mapping's expression callback (`H.make_action` in `lua/mini/surround.lua`). Called directly, it silently reuses whatever you typed last time (I checked: second call with `ds[` still looked for `(`).

So instead of calling `delete()` yourself, call the mapping's callback and return what it returns. You still need some lhs for `mappings.delete`, but it can be a key you never press:

```lua
require('mini.surround').setup({ mappings = { delete = '<F13>' } })

vim.keymap.set('o', 's', function()
  if vim.v.operator ~= 'd' then return '<Esc>' end
  local m = vim.fn.maparg(MiniSurround.config.mappings.delete, 'n', false, true)
  return '<Esc>' .. m.callback()
end, { expr = true })
```

`d` then `s(` / `s[` deletes the surrounding and asks for the id every time. Tested headless on Neovim 0.12.6 with mini.nvim at 24cf4ad.
